summary: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which identified no deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02); it is therefore assessed at the national score. The dossier's only Aguascalientes-specific findings are resident-facing: Human Rights Watch (March 2025) lists it among states that have not reformed their legislation at all to create a legal gender recognition procedure, and it has no enacted state-level non-discrimination protection on sexual orientation or gender identity (a February 2025 initiative was still only an initiative). No region-specific incident, enforcement or ordinance evidence was found.

Guardian global-development report (24 July 2024) on Mexico City making transfemicide a criminal offence - the country dossier uses this reform benchmark to contrast the capital and pioneer states with the non-reforming majority, which includes Aguascalientes.

localsOnly: No state legal gender recognition procedure has ever been enacted here (listed by HRW in March 2025 among states that have not reformed at all), and state anti-discrimination protection for sexual orientation and gender identity remains an unpassed initiative (February 2025) - both resident-facing gaps that do not move a visitor's deviation from the national position.
